ground_truth.description: BaseAuth.recoverSapientSignature returns bytes32(uint256(1)) instead of actual signer imageHash, violating ISapient interface. Breaks Merkle leaf construction in BaseSig.recoverBranch.
ground_truth.root_cause: BaseAuth.recoverSapientSignature returns bytes32(uint256(1)) instead of actual signer imageHash, violating ISapient interface. Breaks Merkle leaf construction in BaseSig.recoverBranch.
ground_truth.attack_scenario: Wallet uses another wallet as sapient signer → signature validation fails due to incorrect image hash. PoC: Add test to test/modules/BaseSig.t.sol: test_BaseAuth_recoverSapientSignature_ReturnsConstant. Deploys MinimalSapient, crafts signature, asserts constant return.
ground_truth.fix_description: Return actual image hash from recoverSapientSignature. Extend signatureValidation to return imageHash or call BaseSig.recover.

vulnerabilities.explanation: The function returns a constant bytes32(uint256(1)) instead of the actual signer image hash, violating the ISapient interface specification. This breaks downstream logic that expects the correct image hash for Merkle leaf construction.
vulnerabilities.attack_scenario: When a wallet uses another wallet as a sapient signer, BaseSig.recoverBranch will fail to construct the correct Merkle leaf because it receives the constant value instead of the actual image hash. This causes signature validation to fail, preventing legitimate operations.
vulnerabilities.suggested_fix: Return the actual image hash by calling BaseSig.recover to extract it, similar to how signatureValidation does. Replace 'return bytes32(uint256(1));' with proper image hash retrieval.

prediction.overall_explanation: The contract contains a clear logic error in recoverSapientSignature where it returns a hardcoded value instead of the required signer image hash. This breaks the sapient signer flow and prevents legitimate signature validation. Other functions appear correctly implemented.
